transcript:
[00:00] Lena Park: hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Lena from Redwood Inference, AE on this account. quick roll call?
[00:08] Maya Torres: Maya here, Head of ML at BlueWave. Evan's on with me and Priya from security.
[00:12] Evan Liu: Evan, platform eng. thanks.
[00:14] Priya Patel: Priya, security manager.
[00:16] Rajesh Nair: Rajesh from Redwood SE, I'll dig into benchmarks and infra.
[00:20] Lena Park: goal for today is to scope the POC — decide whether you should start hosted, reserve dedicated capacity, or go private/VPC, and nail success criteria and timing.
[00:30] Maya Torres: yep, high level: we run clinical triage assistant and summarization across internal notes and patient-reported data. primary concerns: latency (patient UX), cost, and PHI handling. we want to know what makes sense for a 3-month pilot and then production.
[00:45] Rajesh Nair: understood. can you share expected QPS and average prompt length? those drive model choice and deployment mode.
[00:52] Maya Torres: rough numbers: peak 120 reqs/sec, sustained 40 qps, average input 600 tokens, average generation 150 tokens. concurrency of active users around 250-300.
[01:05] Rajesh Nair: great — that profile is helpful. for 600+150 tokens you'll see different memory/KV cache behavior; hosted can handle it but cost and p99 latency depend on batching and prefix cache. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower unit cost if you commit. Private is mainly for regulatory / data residency and on-prem constraints.
[01:25] Priya Patel: on privacy: PHI cannot leave our VPC unless we have guaranteed encryption and audit logs, and we need SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 artifact availability. any support for KMS/HSM?
[01:36] Lena Park: yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations, audit logs, and we can map SOC2 artifacts. Hosted offers a compliant offering too but for PHI many customers pick Dedicated or Private to control networking. we will include security pack in the SOW.
[01:50] Maya Torres: ok, what are realistic latency numbers for p95 and p99 for a 512-1k token request on hosted vs dedicated?
[01:58] Rajesh Nair: ballpark: on hosted with our optimized models (redwood-v4-family, 4-bit quantized) and continuous batching, p95 ~120-200ms for generation tokens per step is tricky to quote; end-to-end p99 for 1k token runs may be 900ms-1.5s depending on load and batching. Dedicated on A100 80GB with tuned kernel selection: p99 can be ~300-600ms for the same work since you avoid noisy neighbors and can set batch sizing for throughput. Private on-prem depends on your hardware; if it's H100 80GB you'll be similar to dedicated. these are rough, we need benchmark runs.
[02:40] Evan Liu: those hosted p99 numbers look optimistic, we're sensitive to p99 spikes. can we run a worst-case tail test?
[02:46] Rajesh Nair: absolutely — bench plan includes tail latency testing under bursty traffic. we recommend synthetic traffic plus replay of 1k real prompts you provide.
[02:55] Lena Park: success criteria — let's define 3 categories: latency (p99 < 1s for 75% of prompts), throughput (sustain 100 qps with p95 under 300ms for short prompts), and cost (target token cost <$X per 1M tokens, TBD after we pick models). also quality: human eval pass rate >= 90% on your acceptance set. does that align?
[03:20] Maya Torres: yes, the p99 <1s is reasonable for pilot. for cost we need a clear per-token estimate. and quality we will provide golden outputs for 500-1k prompts.
[03:30] Priya Patel: also include audit log retention and SSO/SAML for user access during the pilot.
[03:36] Lena Park: noted. we'll include RBAC and SAML integration options in the SOW.
[03:40] Rajesh Nair: on workload sizing — with your numbers I'd propose a pilot using a single dedicated pool of 4x A100-80GB nodes to simulate production throughput; for hosted we can route a subset of traffic and reserve burst capacity. For private, we'll size to your cluster spec once you share VM/GPU details.
[04:00] Evan Liu: any guidance on model quantization and accuracy tradeoffs? we care about hallucination rates for clinical text.
[04:07] Rajesh Nair: yes — we can run evaluations across model variants: fp16, 8-bit, and 4-bit quantized. typically 4-bit offers large cost savings but we will measure delta on your eval set. our Optimize team can recommend quant profiles per workload.
[04:24] Maya Torres: timeline? how long to spin up a bench and deliver results?
[04:28] Lena Park: proposed 6-week POC: week 1 scoping + SOW, week 2 provision infra + network setup, week 3 run baseline benchmarks (hosted + dedicated), week 4 tuning (batch sizes, KV cache, quantization), week 5 extended workloads and security review, week 6 results + decision. if Private on-prem we may add 1-2 weeks for install.
[04:50] Priya Patel: for Private deployments we need an on-site install window and checklist.
[04:53] Rajesh Nair: we'll provide an on-prem runbook including whitelists, ports, CPU/GPU drivers, and an air-gap plan if needed.
[04:59] Maya Torres: what's the cost delta between hosted and dedicated for a pilot with our volume? rough numbers are fine.
[05:06] Lena Park: rough example: hosted invoices per-token + request overhead; for your volume hosted may cost 2-3x more than committed dedicated unit cost. dedicated monthly reserved (4x A100s) with partial commit typically lowers per-token by ~40-60% depending on utilization. exact math in SOW.
[05:22] Evan Liu: is there an option to start hosted for initial validation then move to dedicated?
[05:26] Rajesh Nair: yes that's common. Redwood supports predictable rollouts and can pin model versions to avoid regressions. also can route by policy with automated fallbacks.
[05:34] Priya Patel: audit and logging requirements — we need tamper-evident logs, retention for 1 year, and integration with our SIEM.
[05:41] Lena Park: we can export logs to your S3 or SIEM, support retention settings and include forward-compatible hashes for tamper evidence. we'll detail this in security pack.
[05:52] Maya Torres: for benchmarks, we want both latency/throughput and quality metrics. can you run A/B between open models and tuning LLMs?
[05:59] Rajesh Nair: yes — we'll include A/B lanes and model variants. we'll run generator-only, caching-enabled, and batching-optimized runs. we'll also collect token-costs and per-request cost estimates.
[06:12] Lena Park: Anything else we should capture now?
[06:16] Maya Torres: uptime and SLA expectations — for pilot we need 99.5% availability; for production likely 99.9 with dedicated.
[06:24] Rajesh Nair: we can commit SLA details in Dedicated contracts. Hosted has standard terms; Dedicated adds SLA-backed uptime and response windows.
[06:32] Evan Liu: network egress and data residency: some data must reside in us-west-2. can Redwood provision Dedicated in that region?
[06:40] Lena Park: yes we have capacity in us-west-2; Private on-prem is also possible if you need full residency.
[06:45] Priya Patel: main blockers: we need the security questionnaire answered and legal to review a pilot DPA.
[06:50] Lena Park: we'll attach our DPA template and security questionnaire answers in the SOW packet.
[06:55] Rajesh Nair: benchmark specifics: we'll run a three-phase bench: 1) baseline single-node latency and quality, 2) scale test for throughput and tail under sustained load, 3) mixed workload with caching & burst patterns. please share the 500-1000 sample prompts and acceptance labels.
[07:18] Maya Torres: we'll get that over by Monday.
[07:22] Lena Park: wrap up recap: Lena will send SOW + pricing, Rajesh sends bench harness, Maya provides prompts, Evan shares network whitelist, Priya confirms compliance list. propose bench run week of 2026-03-02. any objections?
[07:38] Evan Liu: sounds good.
[07:40] Priya Patel: no objections.
[07:42] Maya Torres: agree. thanks.
[07:44] Lena Park: great, thanks all. we'll follow up with calendar invites and the SOW.
[07:50] (call ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings — model names like "redwood-v4" may appear as "redwood four" in the raw transcript; timestamps roughly every 30-60 seconds.

Shared artifacts referenced: "Redwood POC playbook" (link: https://app.redwood.ai/poc-playbook), "security pack" (link: https://app.redwood.ai/security-pack), sample SOW template (link: https://app.redwood.ai/sow-template).
